questions.prompt: X @ W_q has shape (2, 10, 64) and there are 8 heads. Which code gives correct per-head queries?
questions.explanation: Split the feature axis first, giving (B, T, H, d_head), then move heads in front of time. Reshaping straight to (B, H, T, d_head) has the right shape but mixes tokens and features across heads.

questions.prompt: With RoPE, the score between a query at position 12 and a key at position 9 equals the score (same q and k vectors) for which pair?
questions.explanation: Rotated dot products depend only on the offset m − n. 12 − 9 = 3 − 0 = 3. The pair (9, 12) has offset −3, which is a different rotation.
Position has to affect only the q·k scores. Values carry content into the output, so they are left unrotated.

questions.prompt: Someone computes θᵢ = 10000^(−i/d) instead of 10000^(−2i/d). Which test would catch it?
options: Checking the frequencies against known values
Checking that RoPE preserves vector norms
Checking that q·k depends only on m − n
questions.explanation: Any θ still gives a rotation, so norm preservation and the relative-position property both still hold. Only comparing against the exact formula exposes the wrong frequencies.
